nt: A **wilderness** is a kind of dry, remote, uncultivated area. If your readers would not be familiar with what a wilderness is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [in the barren region of Sinai] or [in the remote desert of Sinai]
The implication is that **one** means “the first day” of the second month. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on the first day]

The word **one** here means “first.” Hebrew sometimes uses cardinal numbers (1, 2, 3) where other languages would use ordinal numbers (first, second, third). If your language does not use cardinal numbers this way, you can use an ordinal number instead.

The **second month** of the Hebrew calendar includes the last half of April and the first half of May on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar, which is “Iyar” here, then say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

The words **second month** and **second year** use ordinal numbers (first, second, third). Some languages use cardinal numbers (1, 2, 3) in these situations. If your language does not use ordinal numbers this way, you can use cardinal numbers instead.

Here and throughout this chapter, the term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly. For more information, see the book introduction.

nt: The phrase **Lift up the head of** is a common expression of this culture to mean “count” or “take a census of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [count the number of] or [record the total of]
The command **Lift up** is plural here because God is speaking to both Moses and Aaron. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The implication is that **all** refers specifically to the men, as shown later in the verse by “every male.” You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [all the men of]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is characterized by being **the sons of Israel**. If your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the congregation that consists of the sons of Israel]

This is the first of many times in this book that **sons of Israel** refers to the Israelite nation or people group who descended from **Israel**. See the discussion of how to translate this phrase in the [book introduction](../front/intro.md).

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrase **house of their fathers** refers to largest divisions within a single tribe. The word **clans** refers to the largest divisions of each **house of their fathers**. Alternate translation: [according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers made up of those clans]
Here, **house** refers to people who are related. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to the family groups of]
Yahweh is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their ancestors]

The implication is that Moses was to write down the name of each man as he counted them, creating a list or record. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [by listing the names of each one counted]

Yahweh is using **skulls** to represent whole persons. He means that each person should be counted only one time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [counting each person] or [one by one]
